t: The Federal People's Republic of Yugoslavia was proclaimed on 29 November 1945 after an election in which the People's Front took an average of 85% of the vote; it was renamed the Socialist Federal Republic in 1963.

Expelled from the Cominform on 28 June 1948, Yugoslavia steered between the blocs: it refused the Warsaw Pact and NATO alike, co-founded the Non-Aligned Movement and introduced workers' self-management in June 1950.

After Tito's death on 4 May 1980 debt, inflation and nationalism overwhelmed a collective presidency; the League of Communists dissolved in January 1990 and four republics declared independence between June 1991 and April 1992.
dyk: The Cominform chose 28 June 1948 to expel Yugoslavia: the anniversary of the Battle of Kosovo Field in 1389, the assassination of Archduke Ferdinand at Sarajevo in 1914 and the Vidovdan Constitution of 1921.
ev: On 29 November the Constituent Assembly abolishes the monarchy and proclaims the Federal People's Republic of Yugoslavia, a one-party state of six people's republics.
On 28 June the Cominform expels Yugoslavia for 'nationalist elements' and 'Trotskyism'; Soviet troops mass on the Hungarian border and 16,000 suspected Cominformists go to Goli Otok.
Workers' self-management is introduced: workers' councils manage enterprises and share their profits.
A new constitution renames the state the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia; emigration of workers is legalised and Western travel opens.
The third constitution gives the republics and the provinces of Kosovo and Vojvodina wide autonomy; Tito is elected President-for-life.
On 4 May Tito dies; a collective presidency rotating among the republics takes his place as the foreign debt mounts.
The League of Communists of Yugoslavia dissolves along federal lines; multi-party elections bring separatist parties to power outside Serbia and Montenegro.
On 27 April the Federal Council adopts the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia for Serbia and Montenegro, formally ending the breakup.

f.founder: Josip Broz Tito and the Anti-Fascist Council for the National Liberation of Yugoslavia (AVNOJ)
f.predecessor: The Kingdom of Yugoslavia, occupied by the Axis in 1941; Democratic Federal Yugoslavia, proclaimed by the AVNOJ at Jajce on 29 November 1943
f.successor: Slovenia, Croatia, Macedonia, Bosnia and Herzegovina and the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia (Serbia and Montenegro), recognised as five successor states
